Subject: Questions on private deployment DPA, subprocessors, and key control

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we move ahead with a pilot we need to confirm a few privacy and data boundary items for an on-prem (air-gapped) deployment or VPC-hosted private instance:

- Who are Redwood's subprocessors for the private stack (control plane, monitoring, build artifact storage)? Any EU data transfers or US-based subprocessors?
- For VPC and on-prem options: can Acme hold the KMS/HSM keys (customer-managed keys), and what parts of the runtime would still be able to see plaintext (if any)?
- What is Redwood's emergency access / break-glass policy — do you retain administrative paths that could decrypt customer data?
- Can you provide a short DPA/Annex that reflects on-prem controls and a suggested clause for cross-border transfers and restricted subprocessors?

If you can send a short write-up and any diagrams, that would help our security team triage.

Best,
Jennifer

Hi all — quick technical reply to the custody and plaintext questions:

1) On-prem (air-gapped) package:
- Full control: customer-owned KMS/HSM. All model weights, token streams, and KV cache remain on customer infrastructure.
- Redwood operator artifacts: we provide install packages and support access via customer-approved bastion or VM image; we do not ship logs off-prem by default.
- Emergency support: a break-glass session requires an encrypted support bundle provided by the customer and explicit signed authorization; we cannot decrypt without key material provided by customer.

2) VPC private deployment:
- Typical setup: customer VPC with private subnets; some control-plane meta-services (cluster management, autoscaler, image registry access) may run in Redwood-managed control plane endpoints that have network-restricted connectivity to the customer's VPC via VPC peering or PrivateLink.
- Data plane: inference runtime runs in customer VPC and uses customer-managed KMS where possible. For customers that cannot host KMS, we offer a dedicated KMS in the same region under strict contractual limits (no plaintext export).
- Subprocesses: for VPC we may use CDN/build registry and a limited set of monitoring partners for telemetry ingestion; those partners are covered under SCCs and limited processing agreements.

3) Plaintext access: under normal ops, neither Redwood engineers nor subprocessors have access to request-level plaintext for on-prem instances. For VPC with customer KMS, same guarantee holds. The only exception is a customer-provided support session where customer explicitly shares ephemeral key material.

I'll attach a diagram of the KMS/key flow and a short list of current subprocessors (as of today) to the shared Drive link Soojin mentioned.

—Marcus
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on private deployment DPA, subprocessors, and key control

Jennifer — I drafted suggested DPA language and a short subprocessor limitation clause for on-prem/VPC customers. Key excerpts below (see attached doc for full wording and tracked changes):

- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and 30 days' notice before adding new subprocessors that will process customer content. For private on-prem deployments, monitoring and telemetry subprocessors are optional and disabled unless explicitly consented to in writing.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood will not transfer customer personal data outside the EU for accounts designated as EU-data-resident without customer's prior written consent. Where transfers are necessary for Redwood-managed control plane operations, we will ensure appropriate safeguards (SCCs + additional contractual guarantees).
- Key custody & access: For on-prem deployments, customer retains sole control of KMS/HSM and cryptographic material; Redwood personnel will not have keys or plaintext access unless a customer-provided encrypted support token is supplied for a narrow, time-bound support action.
- Emergency access: Break-glass requires a documented request, two-person approval (customer and Redwood security lead), and audit logs are retained for 7 years; all actions are recorded and evidence supplied to the customer.

If this aligns with Acme's expectations we can create an annex and run it through your legal team.

Best,
Lauren
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
